headline: Approved a letter of support for the Walk/Bike Bridge grant; tabled traffic evaluation process discussion until December.
summary: Public comments covered a sidewalk request on Green Mountain Drive and 24 streetlights that are out. A planned crosswalk at Dorset Street and Songbird Road was presented, with construction expected to begin in Summer 2027. Speakers also raised East Terrace safety concerns, and the draft FY26 annual report was reviewed for edits.
decisions: Approved the previous meeting minutes with noted edits, passed unanimously.
Tabled discussion of the traffic evaluation request process until December.
Approved the Walk/Bike Bridge Grant letter of support as written, passed unanimously.

decision_titles: Walk/Bike Bridge Grant letter of support
plain_text:
Page 1 
Bicycle and Pedestrian Committee 
October  14, 2026  
 
The Bicycle and Pedestrian Committee held a regular meeting on October 14, 2026 at 5:30 
pm, in Room 301 of City Hall and by Zoom.  
Committee Members Present (R=Remove): Bob Britt, Ken Burkman, Havaleh Gagne, 
Donna Leban, Mark Passanen, Kim Maxwell, Joshua Minot, and Freeman Stein (R).  
Also present: Erica Quallen Towle (City Staff), Andrew Chalnick (City Council Liaison), Ryan 
Doyle, Jack Evans, Will Flender, Silken Kerschner (City Staff), Kelly LaVigne (Hoyle Tanner), 
Zachary Roussel (Hoyle Tanner), Matt Van Wagner, Craig (last name withheld) 
 
 
1. Welcome, Emergency Exit and Virtual Meeting Instructions, Gratitude 
2. Additions, Deletions, or Changes to the Agenda 
3. Comments and questions from the public not related to the agenda 
a. Green Mountain Drive. 
i. Will Flender asked about a sidewalk project on Green Mountain 
Drive, which is near the UVM horticultural farm. He explained that he 
previously asked about it about a year ago, and again in March and 
was told it’s being considered for prioritization with other projects.  
ii. Donna observed the street is very wide and suggested alternative, 
cheaper solutions, such as bollards or striping. 
iii. Erica explained it has been on the list of traffic evaluation requests 
since April 2023 and undergone initial scoring, which includes length, 
traffic volume, 5-year bicycle and pedestrian crash history, and 
proximity to a school, employer or large retail center. Currently, it 
doesn’t meet the threshold to move forward for next steps, which 
would include design.  
iv. It scored 25, and 25 is the minimum score required to be considered 
for further study. 
v. Will explained he felt the process was opaque and the 
communication was lacking.
Bicycle and Pedestrian Committee – October 14, 2026 | Page 2 
b. Ryan expressed frustration that school officials made stormwater 
management plans for the parking lot north of Tuttle Middle School and 
near the Barrett St connecting path without oversight or interdiction for safe 
bicycle and pedestrian traffic. He also noted that 24 streetlights are out 
between the high school and East Ter, and that some have been out for two 
years.  
c. Erica and Donna explained that some lights are owned by the city, while 
others are owned by Green Mountain Power or VTrans.  
d. Erica will follow up with the city’s lights employee to ask him to follow up, 
prioritizing lights near schools. Jack offered to help identify lights that are 
out, rather than wait until the city employee can do it (who does this work 
twice a year). 
4. Consideration of Minutes 
a. Bob motioned to approve the minutes with noted edits, and Ken seconded. 
The minutes were approved unanimously. 
5. Dorset Street and Songbird Road Crosswalk Informational Meeting 
a. Kelly from Hoyle Tanner presented the project, its proposed layout. Donna 
suggested asking GMP to move and make brighter the light at the 
southwest corner of the intersection, because it currently emits less than 10 
lux, which is the minimum here. 
b. Ryan asked whether there will be a light to frontlight the crossing for 
northbound traffic. Hoyle Tanner will provide the plan details to DPW to 
confirm. 
c. Jack showed a new design for a Rectangular Rapidly Flashing Beacon 
(RRFB) that is designed to cast its light to illuminate the crosswalk. He also 
proposed angling the crossing to allow longer traffic, like bikes with kid 
trailers, to make the turn easily and safely. 
d. Ryan also proposed a minor redesign on the west side of the crossing to 
better protect bicycles and pedestrians waiting to cross. Hoyle Tanner will 
explore this proposal with DPW.  
e. Construction is expected to begin Summer 2027. 
6. Draft FY26 Annual Report Review 
a. Erica solicited edits and noted the report is due in two weeks. 
b. Bob asked to add the Bike Rodeo from August 2025, the Energy Festival. 
Bob also recommended adding the city’s count of xxx in the quantitative 
section.
Bicycle and Pedestrian Committee – October 14, 2026 | Page 3 
c. Havaleh recommended adding the committee’s vision to make it possible to 
safely roll or walk from Burlington city center to South Burlington city 
center. 
d. The committee needs to update its member photo 
7. East Terrace Discussion 
a. Josh noted recent safety concerns with East Terrace, particularly given how 
it will become increasingly important once the pedestrian bridge opens. 
b. Erica announced a new 25 mph speed limit sign has been posted at the 
street entrance. 
c. Havaleh reported a traffic evaluation request was submitted, but that it did 
not meet the threshold for further consideration, even after it was updated 
from 8 to 18. Erica recommended the city not prioritize East Ter over other 
areas that also need improvement, simply because the street was a city 
council agenda item. 
d. A Right of Way permit is needed to apply to Local Motion to use its bump 
outs. 
8. Traffic Evaluation Request Process Review 
a. Discussion was tabled for December, including how to prioritize projects. 
b. The committee will add few other items to the December agenda to ensure 
sufficient time for discussion. 
9. Walk/Bike Bridge Grant Letter of Support 
a. Ken motioned to approve the letter as written, and Mark seconded. The 
motion was passed unanimously. 
10. Safe Routes to School (SRTS) Sub-Group Updates. Jack will share insights from 
the national SRTS conference at the November committee meeting. 
a. Sub-Group Updates (DRB, Safety, Communications and Outreach)- nothing 
to report 
11. Confirm Next Meeting will be Wednesday, Nov 18th at the library conference room. 
12. Adjourn 
 
Ken Burkman - Clerk
